finalText:
**Found it and fixed it.** The leak was in `src/jobs/processOrder.js`.

It grabbed a connection, ran the order, then released. When an order failed, the release line never ran, so that connection was gone for good. The pool has no reclaim, so a failure was permanent.

The worker log shows exactly this ratchet:

```
02:06:15 ERROR job order-4122 failed: invalid order payload
02:06:15 WARN  [db] pool in-use: 3/5
02:06:20 ERROR job order-4123 failed: invalid order payload
02:06:20 WARN  [db] pool in-use: 4/5
```

Only failures moved the count up. Once it hit 5/5, everything got `pool exhausted` and the supervisor restarted things.

`processOrder` now goes through `withConnection`, the same wrapper the request path uses. It releases in a `finally`, so failures give the connection back.

All 4 tests pass, 69ms.
